name: DNA cross-link repair 1C

function.text: DCLRE1C encodes protein artemis. Annotated molecular activities include endonuclease activity and 5'-3' exonuclease activity. It participates in telomere maintenance and interstrand cross-link repair.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to severe combined immunodeficiency due to DCLRE1C deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal recessive; definitive GenCC assertion from ClinGen. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: DCLRE1C encodes protein artemis. It is required for V(D)J recombination, the process by which exons encoding the antigen-binding domains of immunoglobulins and T-cell receptor proteins are assembled from individual V, (D), and J gene segments. V(D)J recombination is initiated by the lymphoid specific RAG endonuclease complex, which generates site specific DNA double strand breaks (DSBs). These ends are independently repaired by the non homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway to form coding and signal joints respectively.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with severe combined immunodeficiency due to DCLRE1C deficiency (autosomal recessive).
